title_vi: Redis có thể dùng vào những việc gì?

source_snapshot.note: Fetched the pinned commit from GitHub; git rev-parse of the path gives the source map's blob OID. Non-empty source body read; no source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Các lệnh nguyên tử dùng ở đây đúng là nhờ Redis chạy lệnh trên một luồng.
Cách dùng Redis làm bộ đệm: các chiến lược đọc và ghi.
Khóa trên một máy Redis và giới hạn của nó khi có nhân bản.

claims.evidence: Statements were checked against redis/docs at commit 3b030c7ef066c0bb7f88ddec02c784e49783b0f8 (distributed locks, INCR, LMOVE, streams, bitmaps, sorted sets, hashes), read from a partial clone, and against an experiment run on 2026-10-18 with the Ubuntu redis-server 7.0.15 package.

claims.claim_vi: Single-instance lock: SET resource_name my_random_value NX PX 30000; the value must be unique across clients and lock requests; release with a script that deletes only if the value matches (or DELEX IFEQ since 8.4); plain DEL can remove another client's lock; viable where an occasional race is acceptable; Redlock is the multi-instance algorithm.
claims.section: Correct Implementation with a Single Instance
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment showed A's late DEL deleting B's lock and the compare script returning 0 and leaving tokB.

claims.claim_vi: INCR supports the counter and rate limiter patterns; INCR followed by a separate EXPIRE has a race that can leak the key, fixed with MULTI/EXEC or a Lua script.
claims.section: Pattern: counter; Pattern: rate limiter 1 and 2
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment rejected requests 11 and 12 with a limit of 10 per 60 s window.

claims.claim_vi: A list used as a queue is not reliable: a message is lost if the consumer crashes after popping it; LMOVE (or RPOPLPUSH) into a processing list gives a reliable queue, with another client watching the processing list.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment popped j1 and it was gone, LMOVE kept j2 in the processing list.

claims.claim_vi: Stream consumer groups give explicit acknowledgment, inspection of pending entries and claiming of unprocessed messages.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment left 2 entries pending after worker-a read them, XAUTOCLAIM moved both to worker-b, one XACK left 1 pending.

claims.claim_vi: Bitmaps are bit operations on strings of at most 512 MB, enough for about 4 billion bits; BITOP does AND/OR/XOR/NOT and more, BITCOUNT counts set bits; user ids should be incremental.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment counted 6, 4 and 3 (both days) and a bitmap with bit 10000000 set had STRLEN 1250001.

claims.claim_vi: Sorted sets keep members ordered by score and serve leaderboards; hashes store field-value pairs under one key.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment's ZINCRBY moved post:c from 90 to 390 and to the top of ZREVRANGE.

design_notes_vi: Năm thẻ kiểu dữ liệu chia làm hai phần (một phần dọc của Facebook chứa khoảng ba thẻ), mỗi thẻ ghi các cách dùng của nó; bốn ghi chú về chỗ dễ sai khi chạy thử. Tên lệnh không đưa vào chữ của hình. Vẽ bằng scripts/figures.
source_deviations: Source lists ten uses with one structure each and no caveat; the lesson groups them by data structure and tests where each goes wrong (lock released by the wrong client, rate-limit race, lost queue message).

Source says a Redis string can acquire locks among distributed services; the lesson adds, from the Redis docs, that a single-instance lock is only safe while that instance is up and that the token-checked release is required.
Source suggests List for a message queue; the lesson adds that a popped message is lost if the consumer crashes and shows LMOVE and streams with consumer groups.
